chart_m0_sample.png: Two panels on the length of the 28,583 specs in the sample. Left: histogram of n_lines clipped at the 99th percentile, with a sharp peak between 20 and 60 lines and a long right tail, and the mean (91) far to the right of the median (56). Right: normal quantile-quantile plot whose upper tail bends far above the reference line, the signature of a strong right skew (skew 11.4) that motivates non-parametric tests.
chart_m0_tools.png: Horizontal bar chart of spec files per spec tool in the sample. OpenSpec holds 22,132 of 28,583 files (77.4%); the largest tools are shown separately and the long tail of tiny tools is grouped as other tools. Every bar is labelled with its count and share.
chart_m1_sample_full.png: Horizontal bar chart of the sample as a share of the full dataset, by table: spec files 6.1%, code references 7.0%, spec links 10.8% and pull requests 89.0%. The sample is thin for specs and near-complete for the pull-request layer, which the legend explains.
chart_m1_tools.png: Horizontal bar chart of spec files per spec tool in the full dataset. OpenSpec holds 274,955 of 470,795 files (58.4%), followed by speckit (11.6%) and adhoc_other (8.2%); the long tail is grouped as other tools and every bar is labelled with its count and share.
chart_m2_pivot.png: Single bar showing that all 5,992 spec-touching pull requests in the corpus are merged, with an explicit annotation that zero rejected pull requests exist. Because rejection is never observed, the review question Q3 is not answerable and the study pivots to traceability.
chart_census.png: Four panels on the census of 332,168 done references with a resolvable anchor. Top left: 332,168 references have an anchor and 8,746 do not, so the latter are excluded. Top right: status is present 297,822 (89.7%), absent 34,227 (10.3%) and ambiguous 119 (0.04%, five repositories). Bottom left: the missing rate is 17.7% in active change proposals and 9.0% in archived changes, against 10.3% overall. Bottom right: the composition inverts the rate, because 73.5% of the missing references live in archived changes and 26.5% in active change proposals.
chart_m4_discovery.png: Two panels showing that exists_at_anchor is not a boolean. Left: present 361,083, absent 51,979, NULL 22,209 and ambiguous 130; the NULL bar is highlighted because NULL coincides exactly with a NULL anchor_sha. Right: the 51,979 absent references split into 34,227 done and 17,752 not done. A note records that 8,746 of the NULL references are done without an anchor.
chart_taxonomy.png: Horizontal bar chart of the taxonomy of the 34,227 done-but-missing references: 17,799 (52.0%) are clean relative paths, 13,326 (38.9%) are bare filenames and 3,102 (9.1%) are non-file noise such as glob patterns and absolute paths. About 91% are therefore real file references, not malformed paths.
chart_accessibility.png: Horizontal bar chart of the share of accessibility requirement lines that are verifiable, by spec tool, over 97,883 lines from 10,717 repositories. Formal spec tools lead, with OpenSpec at 37.0% of 31,792 lines and speckit at 35.6% of 24,753, while informal or embedded specs trail, with docs_embedded at 8.9% of 11,350. The formal tools are highlighted and named in the legend; tools with fewer than 500 lines are not shown.
chart_m7_calibration.png: Horizontal bar chart of the share of resolved references whose resolved path differs from the path as written, by path shape. Relative paths reach 15.2% and globs 5.6%, whereas bare filenames reach 94.8% and absolute paths 100% by construction, because their resolved path is built from the written one. Only the relative-path rate is a real rename signal, which the legend makes explicit.
chart_outcomes.png: Horizontal bar chart of the outcome of the 1,298 classified done-but-missing references: never 54.5%, deleted before anchor 29.5%, created later 9.2%, renamed 4.1% and other 2.7%. Adding the two absent classes gives 84.0% genuinely absent, which is annotated; those two classes also carry distinct hatch textures so colour is not the only cue.
chart_by_bucket.png: 100% stacked bar chart of the classification by repository star bucket, with totals of 247, 486 and 565 references. The never share rises from 40.9% in 0-9 star repositories to 56.4% and 58.8%, while deleted-before-anchor falls from 46.2% to 29.8% and 21.9%: churn dominates immature repositories and non-implementation dominates mature ones. Every segment above 6% is labelled with its share.
chart_bridge.png: Grouped bar chart of the never rate by repository star bucket, with and without accessibility requirements. Repositories without accessibility requirements move from 30.7% to 39.2% to 53.8% as maturity grows, while repositories with them sit at 53.6%, 62.3% and 60.5%; the accessibility group is higher in every bucket. Values are labelled in one decimal place and the two groups are distinguished by colour and named in the legend.
chart_bridge_repo.png: Box plot with every repository drawn as one jittered point, comparing the per-repository never rate with and without accessibility requirements. The 81 repositories without accessibility requirements have a median of 50.0% and the 56 with them a median of 70.7%; a Mann-Whitney U test over the two groups gives the p value quoted in the subtitle, and a note states that each dot is one repository and that red lines mark the medians.
